summary: Iteration 11 — E2E verification of the new Universal Payment Wallet + Vendor Order Details features. Backend regression: 16/16 pytest tests PASS (test_wallet_iter11.py). Covers /api/wallet/me for customer/vendor/contractor; 403 permission checks on all /api/admin/wallet/* endpoints for non-super-admin (customer & vendor tokens); admin credit + debit round-trip; 422 on empty reason and zero amount (AdjustIn validator); 400 + 'Insufficient wallet balance' on overdraw with balance NOT mutated; admin ledger listing; POST /api/orders persistence of site_location/architect_name/architect_phone/company_name verified via GET /api/vendor/orders; POST /api/orders/{id}/pay-wallet debits, marks order paid, second-pay attempt 400; pay-wallet 400 on insufficient balance; pay-wallet 403 when a different user attempts to pay someone else's order. UI: Admin → Administration → rbac-tab-wallet — 49 users listed, empty reason produced 'Reason is mandatory' toast, valid credit produced 'Wallet credit done · new balance ₹25,050' toast and ledger auto-refreshed (13 admin-wtx-* rows), overdraw produced 'Insufficient wallet balance' toast. Customer: nav-wallet shows wallet-section with balance ₹25,000 and Transaction Ledger; cart-checkout with empty order-address shows 'Site location / delivery address is required'; filling address+architect+company and clicking wallet-checkout-btn returned 'Paid via wallet — new balance ₹23,820' and My Orders now lists paid rows; regular Razorpay demo checkout-btn still returns 'Payment successful (demo mode) — order confirmed'. Vendor: nav-wallet balance ₹25,000; nav-orders shows 4 view-order-* buttons; expanding shows order-details-<id> row with Site Location / Architect / Architect Phone / Company / Items rendered (verified snippet 'Site LocationTEST_iter11 addr wrong-user … Items TEST_prod_7ddb9b × 1 ₹1,000'). Contractor: nav-wallet renders wallet-balance ₹25,000. All required data-testids present. No blocking issues.

issues: Pre-existing hydration warning: platform instrumentation injects <span x-file-name=…> inside <option> children. Non-blocking, cosmetic. Same class of warning noted in iter7/8/9/10 for MaterialCalculator template-select. Fix: wrap the interpolated child in String(...) or use a single text expression without additional whitespace, e.g. <option>{`${u.name || u.email} · ₹${…}`}</option>.

action_items: (LOW) Silence <span>-inside-<option> hydration warning in AdminRBAC Wallet tab user selector (same root-cause as pre-existing warning in MaterialCalculator).
(LOW/nice-to-have) 49 users in the admin adjust-wallet select dropdown will grow unbounded. Consider replacing native <select> with a searchable combobox + server-side search once user count grows.

(LOW) OrderIn.items is `List[dict]` — no Pydantic model validating {product_id,name,price,qty}. A KeyError('price') can occur if a client omits price (observed while writing tests). Suggest an OrderItemIn model with typed fields for a proper 422 instead of 500.
critical_code_review_comments: wallet.py apply_transaction correctly uses an atomic find_one_and_update with `{wallet_balance: {$gte: amount}}` for debit — race-safe. Good.

AdjustIn uses Field(gt=0) and min_length=2 on reason — server-side validation is enforced (422 confirmed). Reason min_length=2 is quite low; consider min_length=3 or a normalized check to prevent 'ok' etc.

pay_order_wallet does NOT roll back the wallet debit if the subsequent orders.update_one fails. In practice update_one won't raise unless Mongo is down, but wrap the two ops in a transactional pattern or at minimum reverse the debit on failure to avoid customer wallet being drained without the order flipping to paid.
OrderIn.items is `List[dict]` — see action item; should be a typed sub-model.

wallet.py migrate() reads legacy `wallet` field and backfills wallet_balance. If a user's legacy `wallet` and new `wallet_balance` diverge (e.g. after any manual DB edit), the migration will only run for users missing wallet_balance, which is correct — but the legacy `wallet` field is not removed, so two sources of truth coexist. Consider $unset of the legacy field after backfill.

AdminRBAC AdminWallet lists ALL users (up to 1000) in a native <select>; no search/filter. Fine for demo, not for enterprise scale. Also, the same user appears with same name (e.g. 'Anil Steel Traders · ₹25,000' repeated) — dedupe or show email in every row.

wallet_transactions collection has indexes on user_id and created_at only. For the admin 'all transactions' view sorted by created_at desc with no filter, a compound index (user_id, created_at) is not needed, but pagination is missing (hard-coded to_list(500)). Add skip/limit or `since` cursor.
